content.title: About
content.content: Gordita is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a thin corn‑maize dough pocket filled with seasoned meat (usually beef, pork or chicken), spices and sometimes vegetables. The dough is made from masa harina, water and salt, shaped into small flat discs, stuffed and then grilled or pan‑fried until lightly crisp.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name "gordita" comes from the Spanish word for "fat" or "chubby", although the final product is usually fairly thin.
In Mexico gorditas are a popular street‑food item, often served with salsa, guacamole and a squeeze of lime.
The dough is traditionally unleavened, giving the gordita a soft, slightly chewy texture.
There are many filling variations, from classic beef to vegetarian options with beans or tofu.
Gorditas are sometimes used as a substitute for tortillas in burritos and tacos.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat filling provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef and pork are good sources of heme iron, which supports normal blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat supplies B12, B6 and niacin, nutrients important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in simple carbs
items.content: Corn‑maize dough contains relatively few simple sugars, making gorditas suitable for moderate low‑carb diets.

items.title: Adds fiber when vegetables are included
items.content: Adding vegetables to the filling boosts dietary fiber, which aids digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Seasonings and sauces used in the filling can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Fatty meat options
items.content: Some fillings use fattier cuts, increasing calories and saturated fat.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: The masa dough may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to corn.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor pathogens; ensure the filling reaches a safe internal temperature.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve gorditas hot, split them open and top with salsa, guacamole, sour cream or fresh lime. They are handheld snacks, but can also be sliced and added to salads, bowls or burritos.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked gorditas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. They can be frozen for up to a month; reheat in the oven or skillet before serving to retain a soft texture.
